To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

filtering of the ultravioletradiation spectrum reduces the heat evolved in the active element of an optically pumped solid- state laser made of neodymium glass, and that the heat evolution in a neodymium glass active element is 8–10% of the stored energy.
the heat evolution in CNP and GLS24 active elements activated with Nd ions, without filtering the UV component of the pump spectrum is 11–14%.
the heat evolved from CNPG, GLSS, and YAG elements was 11–12, 9.6–11.4, and 7–9% of the energy in the capacitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of heat evolution in the active elements of solid-state lasers made from CNPG and GLT24 glasses, and YAG:Nd, pumped with a high-power UV laser.
the development of a new method of determining heat evolution, which is a key characteristic of the active medium in optically pumped solid state lasers.
the determination of heat evolution in the active elements of optoelectronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat evolution in the active element is determined by the spectral composition of the pump radiation and by the active element composition and structure.
the heat evolved in the active element is a function of the energy stored and the spectral composition of the radiation, and the heat evolved without filtration is greater than that with filtration.
the heat evolved in the active element is determined mainly by the heat of the pump radiation absorbed in the active element, and the heat evolved is not affected by the energy stored in a capacitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the heat evolved from the active element is determined by the efficiency of the energy conversion of the pump source and the absorption coefficient of the active element in the region of the pump radiation.
heat evolution from the active element in the process of pumping and laser action is a function of the spectral composition of the radiation used.
heat evolution during the pumping process is not a critical parameter for laser operation, but it is a very important factor for the design of a cooling system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat evolved in the YAG active elements is lower than in the CNPG and GLSG24 ones.
the heat evolved from the active elements is not the same as the stored energy.

the heat evolved in the active element is a function of the pump radiation power, which is determined by the energy stored in a capacitor, and the pump radiation spectrum, which is a function of filter cutoff wavelength.
